Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF)                         A. Author
Request for Comments: 9997                                   Example Org
Category: Standards Track                                   October 2026
ISSN: 2070-1721


                          Updated Edition


                       Example Layout Protocol
                              for Tests

Abstract

   This document shows the layout of the text of an RFC.  Its text is
   at http://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9997.

Table of Contents

   1. Introduction ....................................................1
      1.1. Terms ......................................................1
   2. Lists and Tables ................................................2
   3. Figures .........................................................3
   4. References ......................................................4
   Appendix A. Notes ..................................................5
   Author's Address ...................................................5

   This list MUST stay short.

1.  Introduction

   Clients use the server at https://example.com/ per Section 2 and
   Section 9.  Section 4 of [RFC9998] and Section 1 of RFC 9999 are
   other parts.  See [RFC9998], [RFC1234] and [OTHER] for more, but
   not [NOWHERE].

   Section 3 has figures.

1.1.  Terms

   Client
      A program that sends requests.

   Server  A program that answers requests.  The server MUST
      answer as in Section 2.

   Token  A secret value.

   Endpoint

      A path on the server.

1.1.1.  Details

   This section is too deep for the table of contents.

2.  Lists and Tables

   The client sends these parameters:

   o  The client MUST send a token.

   o  a name,

      with a second paragraph.

   The flow has these steps:

   (A)  The client sends a request.

   (B)  The server answers.

   +-----------+-------------------+
   | Name      | Use               |
   +-----------+-------------------+
   | token     | The server MUST   |
   |           | check it.         |
   |           |                   |
   | name      |                   |
   +-----------+-------------------+

               Table 1: Parameters

   +-------+-------+
   | one   | two   |
   +-------+-------+

   Method Use
   ------ -----------------------
   GET    Reads a resource.

   POST   Creates a resource.

                 Table 2: Methods

3.  Figures

   A request:

     GET /tokens HTTP/1.1
     Host: server.example.com

   A response:

     {
       "token": "abc"
     }

                 Figure 1: A token

   An abbreviated response:

     {
       "token": "abc",
       ...
     }

   A rule in a figure:

     {
       "description": "The token MUST be secret."
     }

   A diagram:

     +--------+       +--------+
     | Client |------>| Server |
     +--------+       +--------+
